I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model only outputs a request that names the tool and its arguments. |
| q3 | Wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". An agent repeating the same failing edit needs a step limit, which also protects your budget. |
| q4 | Partial (M4) | 4 is the right count, but your reason says the model runs the tools itself. The model requests a tool and the program runs it. |
| q5 | Correct | You covered both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to choose its next step. |
| q6 | Partial | A tool's name is only part of it. The model works from the whole description: the name, what the tool does and its parameters. |

You have the loop down. Two things are still open: loops need a stopping condition, and the program runs the tools while the model only requests them.

I also added a learning record (`learning-records/0003-loop-needs-a-stop-and-program-runs-tools.md`) and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` has not been graded.

**Next step:** write the makerspace assistant's loop for one request in three columns: what the model outputs, what the program does, and what goes back to the model. Add a step limit and what the assistant says when it hits it. Then we can move on to context and memory.

Do you want me to grade s1 as well, so you can compare the two attempts?
